title: Microsoft to Launch Copilot Super App This Quarter, Merging Chat, Code and AI Agents
excerpt: CEO Satya Nadella confirmed the unified platform during a July 29 earnings call, promising to combine fragmented Copilot tools into a single interface by end of summer.
body:
• Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella confirmed during the company's July 29 earnings call that a unified Copilot "super app" will ship this quarter, combining chat, coding, and autonomous AI agents in a single interface.
  • The app merges consumer Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Copilot Cowork, and a new agentic layer called Autopilot, addressing long-standing complaints about tool fragmentation.
  • Jacob Andreou, EVP of Copilot at Microsoft, is leading the project, which will support both personal and enterprise accounts with a toggle between them.
  • Key details including pricing, licensing structure, and migration plans for existing subscribers remain unannounced.

Nadella Makes It Official

Microsoft will release a unified Copilot "super app" before the end of the current quarter, CEO Satya Nadella confirmed during the company's fiscal year 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call on July 29. The platform reported $90 billion in quarterly revenue, buoyed by cloud computing and AI services.

https://x.com/tomarbuthnot/status/2083134009115041894

"This quarter, we are bringing these Copilot experiences together, including code, in one super app. This is a major step forward, and I look forward to sharing more soon."

— Satya Nadella, CEO, Microsoft

The announcement puts a firm timeline on plans first reported by Fortune's Sebastian Herrera in late May 2026, and separately confirmed by The Verge's Alex Heath, who published a leaked screenshot of the app's interface. At the time, the project was described as targeting an end-of-summer launch. Nadella's earnings call statement narrows that window to the current quarter, which ends in September.

What the Super App Combines

Microsoft's current AI portfolio is spread across consumer Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Copilot Chat, Copilot Studio, and multiple Windows entry points. The super app aims to consolidate these into four core capabilities under one roof: Chat, Cowork, Code, and Autopilot.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Wwxi9UDZqxE

Nadella described the evolution in three stages. Chat handles questions and content generation. Cowork assists with collaborative tasks across Microsoft 365 applications. Autopilots represent the most advanced layer — autonomous AI agents capable of completing multi-step workflows with limited human oversight.

A proactive AI agent called Scout, built on Microsoft's OpenClaw research, also appeared in the leaked mockup. The feature is designed to surface relevant information before users ask for it.

The app will support both consumer and enterprise accounts. According to Fortune's reporting, a toggle function will let users switch between personal and work-oriented Microsoft 365 Copilots within the same interface. Users will still be able to access individual Copilot tools outside the super app.

Fixing a Fragmentation Problem

The consolidation is driven by user frustration. Sources familiar with Microsoft's internal research told Fortune that customers dislike shifting between the company's various Copilot tools and struggle to see unified value from the ecosystem. Jacob Andreou, who was recently appointed as EVP of Copilot, is leading the effort.

For enterprise IT administrators, the move raises practical questions. Microsoft has not disclosed which licenses will unlock specific capabilities, how consumer and work data will remain separated, which agent actions will require approval or audit logging, or whether the new app replaces existing clients outright or simply aggregates them.

A Crowded Race for the AI Super App

Microsoft is not alone in pursuing consolidation. OpenAI has been combining ChatGPT, its coding tools, and agentic capabilities into a single platform. Google's Gemini recently crossed 900 million monthly active users. Anthropic, Meta, and others are similarly merging chat, code, and agent functionality into fewer product surfaces.

The Western market has historically resisted all-in-one apps compared to markets where platforms like WeChat serve as gateways for messaging, payments, and services. Whether Microsoft can overcome that resistance depends on execution — delivering a genuinely connected experience rather than placing existing tools behind a single icon.

What to Watch

Several questions remain unanswered. It is unclear whether GitHub Copilot will continue as a separate subscription or fold entirely into the super app's pricing. Migration plans for existing Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot users have not been outlined. And while Microsoft has framed the project as "one Copilot," administrators will need to see concrete documentation on data boundaries, compliance policies, and tenant-level controls before committing to the transition.

With hundreds of millions of Microsoft 365 seats worldwide and a massive developer base on GitHub, the stakes are significant. If Microsoft ships on schedule, the Copilot super app could become the most widely deployed AI productivity bundle in enterprise software.
nri_angle: Indian IT professionals and developers who rely heavily on Microsoft's enterprise and coding tools will see their daily workflows consolidated into a single platform, potentially reducing licensing complexity for companies with large India-based teams.
